identity._heritage_note: a deliberate casting choice for a representative South African line-up; not inferred from any name
identity.build: slim and athletic, sharp upright carriage, quick precise movement

face: heart-shaped face, high defined cheekbones, direct dark brown eyes, neat arched brows, smooth deep-brown skin with cool undertone, understated make-up
hair: short tapered natural cut, sponge-curled and sharply lined at the edges, or a low sleek fade

wardrobe.teaching: sharply tailored single-breasted suit in ivory, camel or deep burgundy over a silk shell top, pointed flats
alternates: shirt with rolled sleeves for board work

presence.posture: stands with weight on one hip, one hand marking the axis of a graph, the other loose; turns crisply between board and camera
presence.default_expression: assured and quick, a small knowing smile when a mechanism clicks into place
presence.energy: market-floor sharpness - fast, exact, never flustered

_environment_reference: modern classroom, a clean demand-supply diagram drawn on glass or whiteboard, city light through the window
_environment_note: NOT used for platform imagery - tutors are shot in studio. Owner, 2026-07-28: the student left the teachers in the classroom, so the platform does not show one. Kept only as character reference if a composite is ever wanted.
continuity_anchors: short tapered natural with sharp line-up
_continuity_note: the features that MUST survive every regeneration - if these read the same, the audience accepts it as the same person

negative_prompt: cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, waxy skin, plastic sheen, over-saturated colours, HDR halos, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted ears, text, watermark, logo, subtitles, teeth artefacts, dead eyes, glassy doll eyes, vacant thousand-yard stare, identical catchlights in both eyes, flat matte irises, eyes looking through the camera, mismatched gaze direction, classroom, school desks, chalkboard, whiteboard, notice boards, posters, any writing or notation in frame, invented mathematical notation, holding two pieces of chalk, duplicated props, set dressing, generic stock-photo smile
_negative_note: the cinematic terms are deliberate - image models drift toward a film-still look (grade, motion blur, flare) and then the render stops reading as a photograph

headshot.lighting: large softbox key at 45 degrees, subtle hair light, seamless warm neutral grey studio backdrop
headshot.framing: chest-up, eyes on the upper third, slight three-quarter turn

studio.lighting: two-light studio set: large softbox key at 45 degrees, soft fill opposite, gentle rim light to lift the shoulders off the backdrop
studio.framing: waist-up, centred or slightly off-centre with clean space beside the head for overlaid text
studio.backdrop: seamless warm neutral grey paper, evenly lit, no props, no furniture, no set dressing

_prop_rule: PORTRAITS SHOW NO HELD OBJECTS. The first accessory is always a WORN item, because that is what the headshot and studio prompts render; hands are the least reliable thing an image model draws and an object in them compounds it. Objects this subject teaches with stay listed for environment shots, where a surface can hold them.
_anchor_rule: Anchors describe what is WORN or physically true of this person - never something held. An anchor is the strongest signal in this file, so a held object here puts it back in the hands whatever the prompt says.
_hands_rule: No held objects in any portrait prompt. The original generator inserted accessory #2 into a 'Holding one simple item' sentence regardless of whether it could be held, which is how a beaded wristband, a bangle, a watch and a pencil behind the ear all ended up 'held'. Objects belong in environment shots, on a surface.
